title: HTML: Structure of the Web
description: Establish the foundational skeleton of HTML: understand why HTML is the foundational structural pillar of the web trio, parse DOCTYPE declarations, and construct root html, head, and body tags.

objectives.statement: Assemble a complete, valid HTML5 document boilerplate containing DOCTYPE, html, head, title, and body tags.
Distinguish between metadata elements that belong in head and visible content elements that belong in body.

content.title: The Structural Backbone
content.hook: Without HTML, the web would just be an unformatted stream of binary code. HTML is the skeleton that gives human meaning and machine structure to every web page.
content.context: Every valid web page begins with a standardized document framework. The `<!DOCTYPE html>` preamble triggers modern standards mode rendering, `<head>` holds vital page metadata, and `<body>` houses every visible pixel rendered on the screen.
goals: Understand why `<!DOCTYPE html>` is required on every webpage.
Distinguish metadata in `<head>` from rendered user content in `<body>`.
Construct a syntactically valid HTML document skeleton.

content.title: Document Skeleton Anatomy
content.description: <!DOCTYPE html> -> <html> lang="en" -> [ <head> (metadata, <title>, <meta charset>) + <body> (visible UI, headings, paragraphs, buttons) ].

content.prompt: Arrange these essential boilerplate elements in their proper top-to-bottom nesting order for a valid HTML document:

feedback.correct: Spot on! DOCTYPE comes first, followed by the opening html tag, the head container, the body container, and finally the closing html tag.
feedback.incorrect: Review the outer document skeleton: DOCTYPE -> <html> -> <head> -> <body> -> </html>.

content.title: Key Takeaways: HTML Document Structure
takeaways: Every web page requires `<!DOCTYPE html>` at line 1 to activate standards rendering mode.
The `<html>` root tag encloses the entire document and should always specify `lang="en"` for accessibility.
`<head>` holds invisible metadata like `<title>`, character encodings, and viewport settings.
`<body>` contains all visible content, headings, interactive elements, and media.
